page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 96 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and Nitro hypervisor orchestration. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmark and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both rank in the top tier, alongside top-tier memory bandwidth results of 481.31 GB/sec for large block reads and 242.04 GB/sec for large block writes. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reach 198.12 million operations per second, also achieve top-tier status. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories respectively.

Large language model inference speeds present a mixed profile. While text generation for medium and large models ranks in the top tier, text generation for small models is weak, though prompt processing for the same small model remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-core ratio combined with the ARM64 architecture offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. This configuration is suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and multi-threaded data compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.24xlarge is an ARM64 memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores on the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at 2.8 GHz, it delivers 768.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core) and a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps, without local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations, alongside 198.12 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core metrics and small-model LLM text generation are moderate to weak, the instance excels in multi-threaded tasks, large-model LLM text generation, and memory-intensive workloads. This hardware profile provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications, making it suitable for in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, and large-scale data compilation.
